name: LQER: Low-Rank Quantization Error Reconstruction for LLMs
problem: Low-bit quantization error in LLMs is highly structured, but recovering it needs either expensive gradient-based optimization or irregular memory access patterns.
mechanism: After quantizing W to 4 bits as W_hat, model the residual W - W_hat with a rank-r correction driven by an ACTIVATION-INDUCED SCALE MATRIX: rather than reconstructing the weight error directly, LQER constructs a scale matrix from calibration activations and shapes the singular value spectrum of the quantization error so a rank-r approximation captures it. The computation pattern uses dense GEMMs only - it explicitly avoids the Scatter/Gather instructions that irregular outlier-buffer schemes need - and needs no knowledge distillation, grid search or iterative gradient optimization.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): 'nearly-lossless W4A8 quantization' on various LLMs and six downstream tasks, using 1.36x FEWER HARDWARE RESOURCES than the leading state-of-the-art method (that 1.36x is a resource-count comparison, not a latency measurement). COMPRESSION RATIO: 4-bit weights with 8-bit activations, i.e. ~4x on weights. QUALITY COST: 'nearly lossless' on the six tasks named, unquantized in the abstract. The dense-GEMM-only claim is the practically important part - it is what makes the method kernel-friendly.
